source: Drafted for the macos-arm64-foundation profile on 2026-09-22, updated 2026-09-23, from a Linux workstation: no macOS host executed anything here. Every sha256 below was obtained from the publisher, never guessed. Node, uv, gh and ai-memory come from the publisher's own checksum file or .sha256 sidecar; llama.cpp and Qdrant publish no checksum file for these assets, so each asset's GitHub release `digest` field was read via `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/releases/tags/<tag>` and the asset was additionally downloaded to a scratch directory under $TMPDIR and re-hashed with sha256sum (both agreed). The npm registry tarballs pinned here before 2026-09-26 (codex, mcporter, context-mode, socraticode; claude-code was a fifth until 2026-09-23, when it became a `native` pin whose own checksum_ref records its verification) are byte-identical to what `npm view <pkg>@<ver> dist.integrity` reports, cross-checked by downloading each tarball to a scratch directory and independently sha256- and sha512-hashing it. codex, context-mode and socraticode are also byte-identical to their adoption/pins-linux-x86_64.json entries (the Linux pins file gained its socraticode entry after v2026.09.25.2, later than this file's); mcporter was byte-identical when pinned, but its Linux entry has since moved to a newer version (the exception below). codex additionally carries a `platform_dependency` (claude-code carried one too until its move to the native pin): the darwin-arm64 optional dependency npm itself resolves and installs alongside the pinned wrapper tarball, read 2026-09-23 with `npm view <pkg>@<ver> optionalDependencies` for its identity and `npm view <resolved-package>@<resolved-version> dist.tarball`/`dist.integrity` for its url/integrity, each independently re-downloaded and sha256/sha512-hashed to confirm. It is never installed by trusting npm's own automatic resolution of it (unverified) or by reading back npm's install state afterward (measured directly on this project's own host: npm 11.19.0's `--global --prefix` install writes no lockfile anywhere under the prefix and no package.json `_integrity` field, nests a platform-specific optional dependency under the wrapper's own node_modules regardless of --omit=optional/--no-optional/NPM_CONFIG_OMIT=optional, and overwrites a pre-placed nested copy during its own install pass). adoption/bootstrap-macos.sh's install_platform_dependency instead fetches and SHA-256 verifies the platform tarball itself with the same fetch() every other pin uses, then OVERWRITES the unverified nested copy npm's own install just fetched at the exact path Node's own require.resolve (scoped to the wrapper's own directory, and matched against the exact expected nested path -- never trusted if it resolves anywhere else, since require.resolve's GLOBAL_FOLDERS fallback can point outside the prefix entirely) finds it from, falling back to a top-level alias only when nothing is nested there at all; it then re-verifies both the resolved path and the resolved package's own name against this pin's `resolved_package` before running `npm rebuild` to trigger any lifecycle script the wrapper's own --ignore-scripts install deferred. Versions match pins-linux-x86_64.json wherever the component is the same, except ai-memory (2.3.2 here, 2.4.1 there) and mcporter (0.13.13 here, 0.14.1 there), which stay at their earlier versions until a Mac qualifies the newer ones (tests/test_adoption_bootstrap_macos.py's MAC_PIN_LAGS_LINUX). 2026-09-26 addition, after the v2026.09.26 release: rtk, qmd, repomix, toon, ccusage, headroom, markitdown and serena close the rest of the `token-efficiency` profile's macOS pin gap (6 of its 14 components were pinned here before; adoption/README.md's coverage cell), each at its pins-linux-x86_64.json version. Each was re-verified on 2026-09-26 from a fresh download of the upstream artifact, retained in evidence/artifacts/macos-token-pins-20260926/digest-check.txt: rtk's darwin-arm64 tarball against the v0.50.0 release's own checksums.txt and the GitHub release asset digest; the four npm tarballs (qmd, repomix, toon, ccusage) against `npm view <pkg>@<ver>` dist.integrity (sha512) and dist.shasum (sha1), byte-identical to their Linux pins (the same registry-tarball cross-check the npm pins above use); headroom's and markitdown's PyPI files against the PyPI JSON API's own sha256 digests; serena's commit through the GitHub commits API. qmd's `sqlite-vec-darwin-arm64` and ccusage's `@ccusage/ccusage-darwin-arm64` optional dependencies are documented, unpinned gaps like the `rolldown` note in the mcporter entry's install_note below, not new install machinery. headroom pins its `macosx_11_0_arm64` wheel: headroom-ai 0.37.0 publishes compiled abi3 wheels per platform plus a maturin (Rust) sdist that would need a local Rust build, and that wheel is its only arm64-compatible macOS wheel, so it is what uv installs on Apple Silicon. markitdown pins the same platform-independent sdist as the Linux pin (pure Python; uv installs its py3-none-any wheel). uv resolves both from PyPI and does not check either sha256; each is an independent artifact cross-check that satisfies this file's fail-closed null-sha256 refusal. serena has no PyPI release of its declared 2.0.0.dev0 version, so it repeats the Linux pin's source pin: the 40-hex commit c6fbd1c5932df2494ffa0020af5a9fbe80b82143 on oraios/serena with a null sha256, the one documented exception in this file, as in the Linux pins file. adoption/bootstrap-macos.sh gained the `uv-tool` and `uv-tool-from-git` install kinds, whose two functions are copied verbatim from adoption/bootstrap-linux.sh, and a post-install rtk reminder whose config check is that script's four-entry exclude_commands text check, applied to ~/Library/Application Support/rtk/config.toml, the file rtk 0.50.0 reads on macOS (the rtk entry's install_note); tests/test_adoption_bootstrap_macos.py runs all three functions under a real bash 3.2. None of the eight new version_probe entries starts a server.

tools.checksum_ref: npm view @openai/codex@0.155.1 dist.integrity = sha512-02fAAGyBtlA1zPjEo3kTj/bOSYbPz5DvjLwRZJdV7weFFEDzNFOMjQGmZ/+5CuirYV0hE+AZTrnjzwXYU4AdAQ== (2026-09-22); the tarball was re-downloaded and sha256sum matched adoption/pins-linux-x86_64.json exactly
tools.install_note: Platform-independent wrapper package, identical bytes to the linux-x86_64 pin. On Apple Silicon npm additionally resolves the optional dependency '@openai/codex-darwin-arm64', which carries the real binary; see platform_dependency below for its pinned identity. adoption/bootstrap-macos.sh's install_npm installs this wrapper with --ignore-scripts (codex has no lifecycle scripts of its own, so that is a no-op for codex specifically, but this pin shares the same code path as claude-code below), then install_platform_dependency fetches and SHA-256 verifies the platform tarball itself and OVERWRITES whatever npm auto-fetched, unverified, wherever Node's own require.resolve actually finds it from inside this wrapper -- measured directly (npm 11.19.0): a plain global install always nests a platform-specific optionalDependency under the wrapper's own node_modules regardless of --omit=optional/--no-optional/NPM_CONFIG_OMIT=optional (none suppressed the on-disk fetch for this no-lockfile install shape) or of pre-placing verified content first (npm overwrote it during its own install pass); only overwriting AFTER npm's own install, at wherever Node itself resolves from, survives.

platform_dependency.name: @openai/codex-darwin-arm64
platform_dependency.checksum_ref: '@openai/codex-darwin-arm64' is not itself a published package: npm view @openai/codex@0.155.1 optionalDependencies (read 2026-09-23) shows it as an npm: alias to '@openai/codex@0.155.1-darwin-arm64', the same package name at a platform-suffixed version. npm view '@openai/codex@0.155.1-darwin-arm64' dist.tarball/dist.integrity read 2026-09-23 gives the url/integrity above; the tarball was independently downloaded to a scratch directory and sha256- and sha512-hashed, both matching (sha512 matches dist.integrity exactly).

tools.checksum_ref: https://downloads.claude.ai/claude-code-releases/2.1.281/manifest.json (fetched 2026-09-24) lists platforms.darwin-arm64.checksum = a922981f6f3b55a251ef9f9dbaa0621a5f99cbcb5ca67f8a797476ccfc83f626 and size 220931760. Independent byte check without a new download: the 2.1.281 darwin-arm64 binary that Claude Code's own native updater (latest channel) had already installed on a macOS arm64 host is 220931760 bytes and sha256-hashes to the same digest. A manifest.json.sig sidecar exists but no published Anthropic public key or documented verification procedure is available to check it against, so the manifest's signature itself is UNVERIFIED; treat this pin as byte-verified against a publisher-served copy, not signature-verified. Raised from 2.1.280 (387a5c5dcdbb815085edf0baf79591f9d8894efe922bceaf3d75b1b08055229d, its manifest value, re-hashed from a direct download on 2026-09-23), which superseded the prior npm-wrapper + platform_dependency pin (2.1.278, DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1): the native installer is the reference path, matching the linux-x86_64 pin and ~/codex-ecosystem/bin/bootstrap-linux.sh's own claude-code step.
tools.install_note: Fetch the binary, verify its sha256, then run `"$bin" install 2.1.281`, mirroring pins-linux-x86_64.json's claude-code entry (adoption/bootstrap-macos.sh's own *-native case does this). The installed binary self-manages ~/.local/share/claude/versions and the ~/.local/bin/claude launcher and auto-updates on the latest channel from there; this pin is a floor, not a ceiling: install_native keeps a ~/.local/bin/claude whose --version already reports 2.1.281 or newer (nothing is downloaded or installed) and runs the verified install only when that launcher is missing, older or unreadable. No DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER opt-out is set. 2.1.281 is the floor because its CHANGELOG.md entry (read 2026-09-24) fixes a recursive rm whose target is only command-substitution output, such as rm -rf "$(pwd)", running unprompted in auto and --dangerously-skip-permissions mode. This drops the old npm platform_dependency entirely; the native binary needs no nested @anthropic-ai/claude-code-darwin-arm64 package or install.cjs postinstall copy step.

version_probe.note: The pin is a floor: the native launcher auto-updates on the latest channel, so any version at or above the pin passes.

OBSERVED ARCHIVE LAYOUT (tar -tzf on the downloaded asset, 61 entries): one flat top-level directory llama-b11057/ holding every executable (llama-server, llama-cli, ...) NEXT TO its dylibs (libllama*.dylib, libggml*.dylib, libmtmd*.dylib) -- there is no build/bin subdirectory in this macOS asset. The whole directory is therefore installed into tools/llama-cpp-b11057 and bin/llama-server is a wrapper script that exports DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH to that prefix and execs the real binary, not a bare symlink. Metal embedding acceptance (port 8232, 768-dim) is unrun.

version_probe.note: llama-server prints its build number, not the b-prefixed release tag (evidence/receipts/adoption-macos-hosted-smoke-20260922.json).

tools.checksum_ref: npm view socraticode@1.14.0 dist.integrity read 2026-09-23; the tarball was downloaded to a scratch directory and independently sha256- and sha512-hashed, both matching
tools.install_note: Not part of adoption/pins-linux-x86_64.json: recipes/README.md documents socraticode 1.14.0 with --ignore-scripts as a manual Linux install recipe rather than a pins-file entry (`npm install --global --prefix "$STACK_HOME/tools/socraticode-1.14.0" --ignore-scripts socraticode@1.14.0`). This pin brings macOS the same reviewed version and --ignore-scripts convention, so socraticode is no longer a documented, unpinned skip on this platform. AGPL-3.0-only; --ignore-scripts (this pin's own ignore_scripts:true field, read by install_npm) skips native postinstall/build steps exactly like the Linux recipe. Only a reviewed archive hash, not a claim of a working native codebase-index handshake on macOS.

version_probe.note: No argument parsing at all: every invocation, --help and --version included, starts its MCP stdio server (dist/index.js never reads process.argv; observed 2026-09-25 with socraticode 1.14.0), so the package version is read from npm metadata instead.

tools.checksum_ref: rtk-ai/rtk release v0.50.0: the checksums.txt line for rtk-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz and the release's GitHub API asset digest (`gh api repos/rtk-ai/rtk/releases/tags/v0.50.0`) both give this sha256; the asset (4,122,143 bytes) was downloaded fresh and re-hashed, matching both, on 2026-09-26 (evidence/artifacts/macos-token-pins-20260926/digest-check.txt). Same version and verification method as adoption/pins-linux-x86_64.json's rtk entry, for a different platform asset, so a different hash.
tools.install_note: 2026-09-26 addition to complete the `token-efficiency` profile's macOS pin coverage (6 of 14 before; see adoption/README.md). The archive holds exactly one entry, the bare `rtk` executable with no wrapping directory (listed from the downloaded asset, evidence/artifacts/macos-token-pins-20260926/digest-check.txt), so the existing single-binary tarball installer (`install_single_binary_tarball`) applies unchanged. A host that runs the Claude RTK hook at this pin also needs the four-entry `[hooks] exclude_commands` value from recipes/README.md#native-context-mode-and-hooks in ~/Library/Application Support/rtk/config.toml, the only config file rtk 0.50.0 reads on macOS: its path is dirs::config_dir()/rtk/config.toml (src/core/config.rs:495-498 at the v0.50.0 tag commit), the dirs 5.0.1 crate its Cargo.lock pins resolves that to $HOME/Library/Application Support on macOS whatever XDG_CONFIG_HOME says, and rtk reads no config-path variable of its own (evidence/artifacts/macos-token-pins-20260926/rtk-config-path.txt). There, replace the key's whole value inside the existing `[hooks]` table, and add the `[hooks]` header only when the file has no `[hooks]` table (a second `[hooks]` header or `exclude_commands` key is invalid TOML and rtk silently loads defaults). After installing rtk this script prints a reminder unless that key appears exactly once with all four entries in that file; it never writes the file. `rtk config` prints the file rtk reads on its first line and exits 1 when rtk cannot load it, as the same retained check shows on the pinned Linux binary.

tools.checksum_ref: PyPI JSON API https://pypi.org/pypi/headroom-ai/0.37.0/json urls[].digests.sha256 for headroom_ai-0.37.0-cp310-abi3-macosx_11_0_arm64.whl (13,780,628 bytes), read 2026-09-26; the wheel was downloaded fresh and re-hashed, matching exactly (evidence/artifacts/macos-token-pins-20260926/digest-check.txt).
tools.install_note: 2026-09-26 addition to complete the `token-efficiency` profile's macOS pin coverage. PyPI package `headroom-ai` (repository headroomlabs-ai/headroom) 0.37.0 with the `[mcp]` extra, matching adoption/pins-linux-x86_64.json's version and package spec exactly. url/sha256 above are the darwin arm64 (`macosx_11_0_arm64`) wheel: headroom-ai 0.37.0 publishes compiled abi3 wheels for macOS arm64 and x86_64, manylinux x86_64 and aarch64 and Windows amd64, plus a maturin (Rust) sdist that would need a local Rust build (PyPI JSON read 2026-09-26), and this is its only arm64-compatible macOS wheel, so uv installs it on Apple Silicon -- the arm64 counterpart of the Linux pin's manylinux wheel. `install_uv_tool`'s optional pin `package` field makes the installed spec `uv tool install --python 3.13 'headroom-ai[mcp]==0.37.0'`, exactly recipes/README.md's command. uv resolves the pinned version from PyPI and does not check this sha256; it is recorded as an independent artifact cross-check and satisfies this file's fail-closed null-sha256 refusal. Registered at Codex/Claude user scope with `HEADROOM_OFFLINE=1` and `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` (docs/decisions/2026-09-25-codex-mcp-scope.md's addendum: headroom-ai 0.37.0 enables its usage beacon by default; `HEADROOM_OFFLINE` is its documented no-egress switch, `DO_NOT_TRACK` a second one in case a later release renames it).

The wheel uv actually installs, markitdown-0.1.8-py3-none-any.whl (89,737 bytes, sha256 de7375a50578a39bcbbf13b48c67d99033d988e0ae8ad25af46ed432dbe4cbab, PyPI JSON read 2026-09-26 and the wheel downloaded fresh and re-hashed, matching), is also py3-none-any -- the same wheel installs on every platform, unlike headroom above. install_pin's `*-uv-tool` case (`install_uv_tool`) runs `uv tool install --python 3.13 markitdown==0.1.8` into UV_TOOL_DIR/UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR; uv resolves the pinned version from PyPI and does not check this sha256, which is recorded here as an independent artifact cross-check and satisfies this file's fail-closed null-sha256 refusal.

tools.install_note: 2026-09-26 addition to complete the `token-efficiency` profile's macOS pin coverage, pinning the same commit adoption/bootstrap.md step 4a and recipes/README.md's serena row already install manually. `sha256` is null: kind `uv-tool-from-git` with a verified 40-hex `commit` is the one documented exception to this file's fail-closed null-sha256 refusal, exactly mirroring adoption/pins-linux-x86_64.json's own serena entry -- every other kind in this file still refuses a null sha256. `adoption/bootstrap-macos.sh`'s new `install_uv_tool_from_git` (copied verbatim from `adoption/bootstrap-linux.sh`; tests/test_adoption_bootstrap_macos.py runs it under a real bash 3.2 against a `uv` shim) runs `uv tool install --python 3.13 git+https://github.com/oraios/serena@c6fbd1c5932df2494ffa0020af5a9fbe80b82143` into the same UV_TOOL_DIR/UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR layout `install_uv_tool` uses, then reads back the resulting `uv-receipt.toml` and refuses (exit 1) unless it records this exact commit. `serena --version` printed exactly `Serena 2.0.0.dev0` from a fresh, non-editable install of this commit (adoption/pins-linux-x86_64.json's own qualification); no macOS host has run this script, matching this platform's drafted-not-accepted status.

models.install_note: Round 3h: the llama-embed launchd agent had no -m flag at all (it would restart in a loop, never serving embeddings). Downloaded and verified by bootstrap-macos.sh's dedicated install_embed_model step (not the generic tools[] dispatch above: this is a single raw GGUF file, never an archive to extract) into $ECO_INSTALL_ROOT/state/models/embeddinggemma-300M-Q8_0.gguf. The llama-embed template's -m flag names this same path via EMBED_MODEL_PATH (adoption/hosts/<host>.json or --set). Kept in this separate models[] section, not tools[], so it is never swept into adoption/manifest.json profile-component coverage.
